investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official '/en/concerts' listing page, then one of its own real, statically-linked per-event detail pages. The listing page is real static HTML with per-card data-day/data-month/data-year attributes (no JSON-LD); each event's own detail page additionally embeds a full schema.org JSON-LD 'EventSeries' block with startDate/endDate/location/offers.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://38riv.com/en/concerts exposed 24 real, statically-rendered event cards (each linking a real '/en/concerts/{slug}' detail page). A second plain curl GET of one such detail page (still Level 1 — a plain unauthenticated GET, no JS execution) exposed a complete schema.org JSON-LD 'EventSeries' block with a UTC-offset startDate/endDate, full venue address, and structured Offer pricing nested in its own 'subEvent' array. No escalation beyond Level 1 was needed for either page.

venue_reference: 38Riv (38Riv Jazz Club & Bar), 38 rue de Rivoli, 75004 Paris

identity.notes: The retained listing page's own <title> reads 'Jazz Concerts in Paris | Programme & Bookings – 38Riv' at the venue's own domain 38riv.com. The retained detail page's own JSON-LD 'location' object directly states name '38Riv' and address '38 Rue de Rivoli, 75004 Paris, FR' — an exact match to the address given for this investigation, self-consistent with the domain and page branding.

site_classification.platform: Drupal (page classes include 'page-node-type-page', 'current-alias-en-concerts'; a custom booking/ticketing module — URL/asset patterns 'import_billetterie', '?show_session=NNNN', organizer 'ITABUNA' — not the generic wp-json/Tribe Events pattern seen elsewhere in this project).

title.notes: The detail page's own JSON-LD 'EventSeries.name', stated directly.

start_date.notes: The date portion of the JSON-LD 'EventSeries.startDate' ('2026-08-27T19:30:00+02:00'), stated directly.

time.notes: Unlike most sources already investigated in this project, this source's own JSON-LD startDate carries a genuine, explicit UTC offset ('+02:00') rather than a floating local value — a real UTC-resolvable instant, not merely a local clock time.

end.notes: The JSON-LD 'EventSeries.endDate', stated directly, same calendar day as startDate — a genuine performance end time here (unlike Tempodrom Berlin's endDate, which this project separately found to represent only the last calendar day of a multi-day run), consistent with this being a single-evening series.

source_record_id.notes: This source's own permalink URL slug ('/en/concerts/{slug}'), the site's own canonical path for this event — the same documented judgement already established for tempodrom-berlin-01/badehaus-berlin-01.

event_url.notes: The detail page's own canonical URL, stated directly in its JSON-LD 'url' field.

price.notes: Real, structured Offer pricing (multiple price tiers, EUR) genuinely exists in the retained evidence, but ONLY nested inside the JSON-LD 'EventSeries.subEvent[].offers' array — the top-level 'EventSeries' node itself carries no top-level 'offers' field, so this project's EXISTING, unmodified ingestion/json-ld/parse.mjs normaliseJsonLdEvent() (which only reads node.offers) does not reach it via the zero-code path proven in evidence/offline-proof.mjs. A small, generic addition (flattening 'subEvent' the same way extractJsonLdNodes() already flattens '@graph'/ItemList) would resolve this — see this investigation's own README.md and the final report for the exact change needed. Not required for activation (price is the one optional field_assessment key).

blockers.description: Price is only reachable via a subEvent[]-nested 'offers' array, not the generic top-level flatten path — see field_assessment.price. Does not block activation (price is optional); a small, generic subEvent-flattening addition to ingestion/json-ld/parse.mjs (not built by this investigation) would resolve it for a future build phase.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (page title, JSON-LD's own location/address matching the given venue address exactly).
acquisition_class JSON_LD_EVENT, a resolved supported class, reached entirely at Level 1 (two plain, unauthenticated GETs — no JS/browser execution) with no escalation needed.
Two CONFIRMED PUBLIC data paths retained: the listing page (link discovery) and a real detail page (JSON-LD extraction).

title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE, plus time/end/venue_location also PROVEN DIRECT_SOURCE — genuinely rich, UTC-offset-qualified field coverage, better than most sources already investigated in this project.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own URL-slug permalink, following the existing tempodrom-berlin-01/badehaus-berlin-01 precedent.

recommended_family JSON_LD (title/start_date/end/venue/url all reached with this project's EXISTING, entirely unmodified ingestion/html-link-discovery/ + ingestion/json-ld/ families — only a caller-side widening of extractEventNodes()'s own already-exposed 'types' option, from the default {Event, MusicEvent} to include this source's own 'EventSeries' type, was needed; neither shared module's code was edited).

DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence retained (evidence/offline-proof.mjs + evidence/offline-proof-output.txt), reproducing every claimed field value offline against the retained fixtures using the existing, unedited shared modules.
No unresolved CRITICAL blocker — the one documented MINOR blocker (price nesting) does not block activation, since price is this project's one optional field.

Production wiring (actually registering this source and building any small caller-side configuration) is separate, later, explicitly-authorised work — this investigation only establishes and proves the acquisition path.
